## Status

Accepted. Amended 2026-10-21 (see below).

## Context

GitHub unauthenticated API limits (60 req/hr) are insufficient for public traffic.

## Decision

Implement Apex-based caching via Scheduled Jobs and Custom Metadata.

Prevents site failure by serving a GitHub_Cache\_\_c record when API limits are exhausted.

Commits may appear with a "Last Updated" delay of up to 15 minutes.

# ADR-012: Guest User Security (Restriction Rules)

## Status

Accepted, made real on 2026-10-23 (see the amendment below).

## Context

Standard sharing rules are additive and prone to accidental over-exposure.

## Decision

Implement Restriction Rules on the Testimonial\_\_c object.

## Rationale

Enforces a "Block First" policy for unapproved content at the kernel level, adhering to Zero Trust principles.

## Implications

Operates as a hard filter on record visibility specifically for the Guest User profile.

## Amendment (2026-10-23): the rule now does the filtering

Until 2026-10-23 the guest could not read any testimonial, so `Block_Unapproved_Testimonials` filtered nothing. The testimonial wall needs the guest to read approved rows, so a guest sharing rule, `Guest_Read_Testimonials`, shares every testimonial read only with the guest, and the restriction rule alone hides the unapproved ones.

That this holds is proven, not assumed: `TestimonialGuestAccessTest.theGuestNeverReadsAnUnapprovedTestimonial` runs as the real site guest over the seeded rows. With the restriction rule deployed inactive it fails, because the guest reads the pending row, and with the rule active it passes. `TestimonialController.getApprovedTestimonials` also filters on `Approved__c = true`, so the wall would stay correct even without the rule, and the rule protects every other path a guest could take to the object.

A reviewer noted that the API returns Salesforce record Ids. It is not a security problem. The API runs as a read only integration user, tokens are scoped, and an Id grants nothing by itself. It is a design smell all the same. A public API should expose keys it controls, not the internal row Ids of the system behind it. An Id ties every client to Salesforce, changes when a record is deleted and recreated in another org, and shows a reader the platform and the object from its first three characters.

I chose an additive change to v1, not a break. Nothing is removed. Removal would be v2.

## Decision

**Every object the API exposes gets a stable `Public_Key__c`. The API returns it beside `id`, accepts it anywhere an Id is accepted, and the specs mark `id` as deprecated.**

- **Field.** `Public_Key__c` on 13 objects. Text(24), External ID, unique, case insensitive, not required at the field level, because rows that existed before the field get their key from the backfill.
- **Format.** An object prefix, an underscore and 10 random characters from `abcdefghijkmnpqrstuvwxyz23456789`.

ProjectCardController.getHomeCaseStudies.title: Designing an employer hub for an education provider
ProjectCardController.getHomeCaseStudies.solution: A working Employer Hub demo built on Salesforce. Every inquiry is captured once from a web form, matched to the partner's account and routed by the employer's industry. Service requests are fulfilled from the case, and monetary requests run through an opportunity to a contract. Operations and executive dashboards report from the same records.
ProjectCardController.getHomeCaseStudies.challenge: Several departments at an education provider worked with the same employer partners, each from its own inbox and spreadsheet. Partners repeated themselves, and nobody could see the whole relationship. Leadership had no shared numbers for engagement, investment or hiring.
ProjectCardController.getHomeCaseStudies.businessValue: Designed so that employer partners get one front door and a faster answer, departments stop duplicating outreach and see each other's work with a partner, and leadership can report on the employer relationship as a whole.

ProjectCardController.getHomeCaseStudies.title: Choosing the right platform for a literacy nonprofit
ProjectCardController.getHomeCaseStudies.solution: Advised against Education Cloud, which is built and priced for large institutions. Chose donated Sales and Service licences with free NPSP and Program Management over Nonprofit Cloud, for a cheaper path past ten seats. Left donations where they already ran.
ProjectCardController.getHomeCaseStudies.challenge: A small staff with no full time admin needed one system for students, volunteers and training partners, inside a tight grant budget.
ProjectCardController.getHomeCaseStudies.businessValue: Ten staff users on donated licences, with staff testing the build in user acceptance before production.

ProjectCardController.getHomeCaseStudies.title: Building this site as a production org
ProjectCardController.getHomeCaseStudies.solution: This site is its own delivery evidence. Every pull request is validated in a fresh scratch org with the local Apex tests and static analysis, and every merge that changes the app deploys to production through GitHub Actions and runs the local tests. Each run publishes a governance event that is stored as a pipeline run record. The Delivery page shows the latest run per workflow, the Jira roadmap and the recent commits, read from caches that scheduled jobs refresh.
ProjectCardController.getHomeCaseStudies.challenge: A resume can say someone practises DevOps, but it gives a reviewer nothing to check.
ProjectCardController.getHomeCaseStudies.businessValue: The test count on this card and the checklist on the Delivery page come from those stored runs, so they change when the pipeline does. A reviewer sees the roadmap, the commits and the latest pipeline results on one page.
